title: XBOW Pricing in 2026: What It Costs, How Credits Work and What to Ask
summary: XBOW lists no price on xbow.com. AWS Marketplace lists a $50,000 12-month Attack Credit package. How credits work, what to ask, and alternatives.
body_markdown:
XBOW (xbow.com) does not publish a price publicly. Its pricing page describes usage-based pricing that is scoped to your environment and asks you to request a quote. The one public list price we found is on AWS Marketplace: a 12-month package of XBOW Attack Credits listed at $50,000, with usage beyond the package billed as overage. XBOW's November 2025 launch put Pentest On-Demand at a starting price of $4,000. If you need a fixed price per pentest and an auditor-ready report within 48 hours, for SOC 2 or a customer security review, CodeAnt AI is the better fit; XBOW fits teams with many web apps that want credit-based, continuous testing.


CodeAnt AI has run 12,000 pentests and is trusted by more than 1,000 companies, including Fortune 500 companies like NRG, cybersecurity leaders like Commvault, and fast-growing companies like 11x and Sanas.


> Every XBOW and competitor fact below was checked on the vendor's own page recently.


## How Much Does XBOW Cost in 2026?


XBOW is priced by quote. The pricing page offers "Usage-based pricing that scales with your coverage, not a fixed annual engagement" and says "Pricing is scoped to your environment." It lists no plans, rates or calculator, and the only buttons are Request a Quote and Get a Demo.

By the time this page was first published on July 23, 2026, the pricing page had already stopped listing per-test prices. The $4,000 launch figure is still useful as a negotiation anchor for a single application, but it is not a current price.


## How Does XBOW's Credit-Based Pricing Work?


The AWS Marketplace listing is the clearest public description of the meter. It says:


-


You buy XBOW Attack Credits in packages, and consumption draws down from that balance.


-


"An Attack Credit is the base unit drawn down as autonomous agents test your applications. Consumption reflects the offensive security work performed against your targets."


-


Credits "are used based on the coverage you run, not a fixed engagement window."


-


100 Centi Credits equal 1 Attack Credit, and usage beyond the contract is billed as overage.


-


"All fees are non-cancellable and non-refundable except as required by law."


What the listing does not say is how many credits $50,000 buys, or how many credits one application, one assessment or one retest uses. That is the number that decides your cost, so get it in writing before you sign. Ask XBOW:


1.


How many Attack Credits does a full assessment of one of our applications use, and what makes that number go up (app size, authenticated roles, sequential mode)?


2.


Do retests and the reports you generate yourself draw down credits?


3.


What happens to unused credits at the end of the 12-month term?


4.


What triggers overage, and can we cap it?


5.


Does a private offer through our cloud marketplace change the package price or the credit count?


XBOW's own August 7, 2026 article on AI pentesting cost makes the same point from the other side: AI pentesting "changes the cost model by making testing more repeatable and predictable", but "That does not make AI pentesting cheaper by default." Compare cost per covered application per year, not the headline package price.


## What Was XBOW Lightspeed Pricing?


Lightspeed Plus cost $4,000 per test and Lightspeed Premium cost $8,000 per test until the tiers were retired in mid-July 2026. The $4,000 figure remains verifiable today in XBOW’s own launch announcement, while the $8,000 tier and its value framing survive only in captures of the retired cards.

The tier split keyed on application complexity, with Plus for lightweight apps with simple workflows and Premium for platforms with multiple modules, integrations, and deeper access-control patterns. XBOW’s retired cards equated the tiers to the depth of a 2-week and a 4-week manual penetration test respectively, a yardstick worth bringing to any quote conversation even though the claim no longer appears on live pages.


Both tiers carried the same feature list: an audit-ready report within 5 days, instant re-testing with automated verification, authentication testing covering 2FA and magic links, detailed proof-of-concept exploits, remediation guidance,[black, white, or grey box](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/black-box-vs-white-box-vs-gray-box-penetration-testing) modes, and compliance-mapped reporting. Enterprise stacked on continuous coverage, realtime findings, SSO, API access, and human-directed operatives.


## How Does XBOW’s Usage-Based Pricing Work?


XBOW has published no mechanics, so the levers below follow directly from how it describes its own packaging. Use them to shape the quote conversation.


-


**Coverage.** Usage-based pricing that “scales with your coverage” means every application you add to scope moves the number, and a portfolio of thousands of apps is the explicit top of the range.


-


**Application complexity.** The retired Plus and Premium split doubled the price as modules, integrations, and access-control depth grew, and complexity almost certainly still separates quotes.


-


**Continuity.** Continuous testing on every release was always the Enterprise sell, against one-off on-demand tests. Where you land between those modes shapes the contract, a trade our[continuous vs annual pentesting guide](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/continuous-vs-annual-pentesting) unpacks.


-


**Enterprise controls.** SSO, API access, IDOR testing, human-directed operatives, and data residency all sit behind the Enterprise gate, so needing any of them moves you into custom territory.


Ask sales three questions up front: what unit the meter counts, what happens to the rate as applications are added mid-contract, and which of the capabilities you need are Enterprise-gated.


## Can You Buy XBOW Through a Cloud Marketplace?


Yes. XBOW's pricing page lists AWS, Google, Oracle and Microsoft marketplaces and says buyers can "Buy through agreements you already have and put your committed spend to work." XBOW's AWS page adds that purchases can be applied "against eligible AWS committed spend, including PPAs" and consolidated on one AWS invoice.


For a team with an unspent cloud commitment, that can matter more than the list price: the purchase may come out of money already committed. Check with your cloud account team that the listing counts toward your commitment before you plan around it.


## Does XBOW Have a Free Trial?


Not on xbow.com, which offers a demo and a quote request and no self-serve signup. The AWS Marketplace listing does say "Try this product free according to the free trial terms set by the vendor", without a length or usage limit. If a trial matters to you, ask XBOW for those terms in writing: how many credits, which applications, and whether trial findings come with the same review and report as a paid assessment.


## Is XBOW Cheaper Than a Traditional Penetration Test?


XBOW's launch release made the case itself: a traditional pentest takes "35 to 100 days from scheduling to final report" and often costs $10,000 to $35,000 or more, against a $4,000 starting price and results within five business days. Those were XBOW's numbers for its per-test product in November 2025.


Under the credit model the comparison depends on how many applications you cover and how often. One annual compliance test of one app is a different purchase from continuous testing across a portfolio, and a $50,000 credit package only beats a $10,000 to $35,000 manual test if you use enough of it. Work it out per application per year, with retests and report generation included, before you compare.


Whether the quote you receive preserves that traditional-pentest advantage is exactly what the negotiation now decides. Our[penetration testing cost guide](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/penetration-testing-cost) puts the wider market numbers in one place.

## Is XBOW Worth the Cost for Continuous Application Security Testing?


It can be, if three things are true: most of your risk sits in web applications and their APIs, you have enough applications to use a credit package across the year, and you can buy through a cloud commitment you would otherwise leave unspent. In that case XBOW's free unlimited retests and self-generated reports make continuous testing cheaper to run than booking a firm several times a year.


It is a weaker fit when you need one test for one deadline. A SOC 2 audit, a bank partner's review or an enterprise customer's questionnaire usually asks for a single, scoped pentest with a report, and a 12-month non-refundable credit commitment is a lot to carry for that. It is also a weaker fit when the auditor's scope includes cloud, Kubernetes or internal networks, which XBOW does not test today.


## What Do Buyers Ask Before they Choose Usage-Based Pentest Pricing?


These come up on our own sales calls, paraphrased:


-


"We need one number for the budget." Open-ended usage breaks annual budgets, and enterprise master agreements usually need a final figure for the scope. If you buy credits, ask for a committed package sized to your expected coverage and a hard cap on overage.


-


"Is this a one-off for compliance or an ongoing program?" Buyers often want the first test priced on its own, then a separate price for recurring tests once they have seen the results. Ask any vendor to quote both, and whether volume lowers the price per test.


-


"Who stands behind the report?" Buyers now judge AI pentests on evidence: the request and response behind each finding, a record of what was tested and where testing stopped, and who reviewed it. One buyer we spoke with ruled out a vendor whose deliverable read like a generated document with no test records behind it. Ask for a sample report and the log behind one finding before you sign, and check with your auditor that a report you generate yourself meets what they ask for.What to Watch Before You Sign Up


From XBOW's homepage, documentation and blog, checked November 12, 2026:


-


Findings with proof. "Every finding comes with the working exploit, the request, the response and the steps to reproduce it."


-


Review before delivery. "Findings are reviewed before you see them." XBOW's AWS page says each engagement includes a final review by a human security expert.


-


Retests. "Deploy the fix, trigger a re-test, free and unlimited, and XBOW confirms it closed."


-


Reports you generate yourself. Since November 2, 2026, customers create reports in the XBOW Console or API: a letter of attestation for auditors, an executive summary and a full penetration testing report with steps to reproduce.


-


Scope. XBOW's documentation says it "currently supports testing web applications and their APIs", with other asset types on the roadmap. Internal networks, cloud accounts and Active Directory are outside that scope today.


-


API. The API reference is labelled Preview.


If your audit scope includes cloud, Kubernetes or internal networks, price that work separately, because XBOW's credits will not cover it today. For more detail on the product itself, see our breakdown of XBOW features.

## Where This Leaves You


Budget for XBOW the way you would for any quote-only enterprise tool, with one advantage. Its own press release still says pricing “starts at $4,000,” its own benchmark puts traditional alternatives at $10,000 to $35,000, and those two numbers bracket your negotiation.


XBOW fits when your critical risk is concentrated in web applications, you want autonomous testing with proof, and a sales cycle plus an unpublished rate are acceptable costs of entry. The wider field is mapped in our[XBOW alternatives guide](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/xbow-alternatives) .
